prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1301; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder.
text:
Entry 1: Reported side impact at a signalized intersection. The claimant is not represented and was seen at the scene complaining of back pain. Police attended and confirmed the claimant was seated in the vehicle when it was struck.

Entry 2: Scene photos show the point of impact on the driver side panel and roughly match the description given on the first call. The only other people present were passengers and a passing motorist, and no independent witness has come forward.

Entry 3: Damage to the vehicle appears largely in line with a side impact of the described type. No prior damage to this vehicle is recorded in our file or shown in the photos reviewed.

Entry 4: Claimant reports back strain and attended urgent care the same day. The presentation fits the kind and force of this crash well, and no earlier injury to the same area is known.

Entry 5: When re-contacted, the claimant added a few small details, such as the approach speed and lane position, but the core account has not changed. Coverage records show the policy was in force at the time of loss, and nothing suggests the damage predates it.

Entry 6: The driver is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder. The claimant has given a statement about permission to drive, and verification of that permission is pending.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. The injury component remains under review based on the medical records received so far.
